transcript.text: Just got a new Siemens dishwasher and there's always a bit of water left in the bottom under the filter after it finishes. Is it draining properly?

A small amount of clean water sitting in the sump area under the filter is actually normal; it keeps the internal seals lubricated. However, if there is a large volume of dirty water, or if the machine stops mid-cycle with an error, that indicates a drainage fault. 1. Is the water clean and roughly level with the bottom of the filter housing (about a cup's worth), or is it much higher and possibly dirty?
2. Does the dishwasher finish its cycle normally without pausing or flashing an error code?
[Helpful to see: image "Where the filter is" — The filter sits in the base of the dishwasher, usually under the bottom spray arm. Twist it out anticlockwise and rinse it under a tap. Typical layout — your dishwasher may differ.]
Thanks. The water is clean and only about a cupful, covering the bottom of the sump under the filter, with none in the main tub. The cycle finishes normally with no error codes.

[Heading: Normal operation (sump water)]
Yes, it is draining properly. That small amount of clean water sitting under the filter is normal; it stays in the sump to keep the internal seals lubricated and prevent them from drying out.

candidates.cause: Normal residual water in the sump
